summary: The blueprint is broadly plausible for healthy human pancreas, but should split venous from capillary/fenestrated endothelium and retune the ductal mucin axis away from metaplastic or disease-heavy markers.

issues.description: The current endothelial refinement merges venous and capillary/fenestrated endothelial identities into one module/axis, losing a meaningful expected pancreatic vascular component, especially islet-associated capillary/fenestrated endothelium.
issues.suggested_fix: Split this into separate gated endothelial axes: one capillary/fenestrated/islet-capillary module using markers such as PLVAP, CA4, RGCC, EMCN, RAMP2, KDR/FLT1 as appropriate, and one venous module enriched for venous markers such as ACKR1, VWF, EPHB4/NR2F2 or related venous genes. Keep arterial and lymphatic branches as sibling endothelial refinements.

issues.description: The mucin/secretory ductal module includes several genes more suggestive of gastric/intestinal metaplasia or mucinous disease/injury programs, especially TFF1, TFF2, and MUC5B, which risks over-representing a non-baseline ductal state in a healthy, condition-null pancreas scenario.
issues.suggested_fix: Retune this module toward normal pancreatic ductal/large-duct or secretory duct biology, or explicitly make it a low-emphasis ductal injury/metaplastic state. If keeping a normal mucin/secretory duct axis, emphasize markers such as MUC1, MUC4, TFF3, AGR2, AGR3, CLDN18, ANXA4, CFTR/SLC4A4-compatible ductal markers and avoid making TFF1/TFF2/MUC5B primary drivers.

out_of_scope: I did not check dataset-specific gene presence or expression frequency; this is only a biological plausibility review of the declared modules and axes.
